verdict.summary: Basic sign-in is self-serve. Posting to company pages is gated: only registered legal organizations with commercial use cases qualify, there are two review tiers, and approval is at LinkedIn's discretion.

callouts.text: Community Management API is only available to registered legal organizations for commercial use cases. Personal email addresses won't pass vetting.
Community Management must be the only product on its developer app. If the app has other products or pending requests, the request button is greyed out, so create a new app.
LinkedIn may decline to upgrade a partner even if the minimum requirements are met.
If rejected, you can't reapply with the same app. You must create a new app and start from the Development tier.

steps.title: Create a LinkedIn Page for your company
steps.detail: The developer app must be associated with, and verified by, your organization's Page.

steps.title: Create a developer app
steps.detail: At linkedin.com/developers/apps/new. The app name can't include LinkedIn or Microsoft names or logos.

steps.title: Have a Page super admin verify the app
steps.detail: A super admin of your Page must approve the app association.

steps.title: Add 'Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect' (self-serve)
steps.detail: Request it from the Products tab. Scopes openid, profile, email. Enough for login and basic profile.

steps.title: Implement OIDC sign-in and test
steps.detail: Build the authorization code flow and validate the ID token against LinkedIn's discovery document.

steps.title: (Company posting) Create a separate app for Community Management
steps.detail: Community Management must be the only product on its app. Use the same company Page.

steps.title: (Company posting) Submit the Development tier access request
steps.detail: Provide a verified business email, the organization's legal name, registered address, website, and privacy policy. Complete the vetting survey within 21 days.

steps.title: (Company posting) Build within Development tier limits
steps.detail: 500 calls/app/day, 100 calls/member/day, no BATCH_GET, no webhooks. Finish the integration within 12 months.

steps.title: (Company posting) Record screencast and apply for Standard tier
steps.detail: Record a high-res, downloadable, narrated screencast of each use case (OAuth, posting, how comments and member data are displayed), and provide test credentials.

steps.title: Wait for a decision
steps.detail: No SLA is published. LinkedIn emails your business address if it needs more information.

drafts.note: Templates to edit. Replace every [bracketed] part and describe only what your app really does. LinkedIn checks the legal organization, website and privacy policy behind the request.

scopeJustification.text: [Company legal name] builds [app name], an AI assistant that helps [marketing teams at B2B companies] publish posts to their own LinkedIn company Pages. A Page admin connects their Page, the assistant drafts a post, and the admin reviews and approves it before it's published. We need w_organization_social to publish approved posts to Pages the user administers. We don't post without explicit approval.

[App name] shows Page admins the comments and engagement on posts it published, so they can [reply / see results] without leaving the app. We read only posts and comments for Pages the user administers, display them to that admin, and keep them for [retention period].

demoVideoOutline: Introduce the company and the product in one sentence; show your website and privacy policy.
Show the OAuth flow: click 'Connect LinkedIn', the LinkedIn consent screen with the requested permissions, and the redirect back.
Show each use case end to end: drafting a post, the admin approving it, and the post appearing on the company Page.
Show how comments and any member data are displayed in your app.
Show how a user disconnects and how data is deleted.
Narrate throughout, record in high resolution, and make the file downloadable for reviewers.
checklist: The app is associated with your company Page and verified by a Page super admin.
Community Management is the only product on this developer app (create a new app if needed).
You use a verified business email, not a personal address.
The organization's legal name, registered address and website match public records.
A valid privacy policy is published on your domain.
You stayed within Development tier limits (500 calls/app/day, 100 calls/member/day).
The screencast covers every use case and is high-res, narrated and downloadable.
Test credentials for your app are ready for reviewers.
You know a rejection means starting over with a new app at the Development tier.

communityNotes.tip: The Community Management API has to be the only product on its LinkedIn app, so you can't add it to an app that already has other products. What worked was creating a second app just for it.
